# X5: UI/UX for an interrogation-training arena — interrogation mechanics, avatars, talking agents, companion pets, agents visibly at work

Research date: 2026-10-08. Prior baseline read in full and not repeated: `/Users/balla/Desktop/satvik/2026 Fall/Challenge X/TechnoMile Agentic Black Hat/docs/research/external/E13-ui-ux-state-of-the-art.md` (2026-09-25) — it covers agentic-research-product UI patterns (plan/progress/steer), matrix/graph layouts, the React/shadcn/AI Elements stack versions, Linear/Vercel design language, AG-UI/A2UI transport, and Arize Phoenix deep-link routes. Those are directly reusable for this project's "agent visibly working" panel and component stack and are cited by reference here, not re-derived. This route covers only what E13 did not: interrogation-specific game mechanics, avatars/talking heads, companion pets, and training-simulator UX.

Relevant requirement IDs: PRB-4 (no demeanor/stress shortcuts to deception), SOL-1 (text transcript is the scored artifact; avatar/voice is presentation only), SOL-2/AST-* (assistant coaching contract), SOL-3/SUB-* (subject role-play), SCN-3/SCN-9 (style independent of role; evaluator-only packet), EX-2/EX-3/EX-4 (flag/finding format, synthetic ground rule), EVL-7/EVL-8 (investigator rubric, evasion precision/recall), KPI-4 (coaching within 3s).

## 1. Interrogation and detective-game mechanics

**L.A. Noire vs. Ace Attorney — the direct ancestor of "present evidence against testimony."** L.A. Noire's interrogation UI is a half-circle of three response buttons — Truth (top), Doubt (middle-left), Lie (bottom) — where choosing "Lie" requires tagging a specific piece of evidence that contradicts the subject's statement. The designers have said the system was directly inspired by Capcom's Ace Attorney "Press Statement / Present Evidence" loop. The critical UX difference: L.A. Noire gives **one shot per statement** — picking "Doubt" on a truthful line loses that information permanently and can't be revisited — while Ace Attorney is far more forgiving, letting the player retry a cross-examination until they present the *correct* contradicting evidence, and only locking in progress then. [Game Developer, "L.A. Noire's interrogation system", https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/l-a-noire-s-interrogation-system (referenced via search, undated); Giant Bomb, "A Lesson in Logic", https://giantbomb.com//user-reviews/id/59478/a-lesson-in-logic] — high confidence, corroborated by multiple independent sources describing the same mechanic and the same forgiveness delta.
- **Implication (AST-2, AST-7, EX-2):** our coach is closer to Ace Attorney's retry model than L.A. Noire's one-shot model — PRB-1 explicitly wants *repeated practice adjusting questions*, so a wrong follow-up should not destroy information; it should cost turns (against the 12-exchange cap, BKO-7) and get logged as a coaching teaching moment, not a hard failure state. The "present evidence against a specific statement" interaction (click/attach a transcript turn ID to a flag) maps directly onto AST-7's citation requirement.

**Ace Attorney UX study.** A dedicated UX teardown describes the "Press Statement" and "Present Evidence" dual-mode as the game's core grammar: every witness statement is pressable (asks for elaboration) and, once sufficient contradiction is suspected, presentable against a specific piece of evidence from an always-visible evidence inventory (the "Court Record"). Evidence items are tagged by which statements they can contradict; presenting the wrong evidence produces an explicit, non-punishing "that's not it" response rather than game-over. [UX study on Ace Attorney, https://ghostcms.tenten.co/learning/ux-study-ace-attorney-en/ (undated)] — medium confidence (single source, not independently cross-verified, but consistent with widely known game design).
- **Implication:** an always-visible "evidence/case-facts inventory" panel, with each item showing which statements it can be matched against, is a reusable pattern for our **evidence board** — and it naturally supports SCN-4 (evidence released on a script): items simply appear in the inventory as the scenario controller releases them.

**Her Story / Telling Lies and Return of the Obra Dinn — trustworthy-UI and deduction-fairness principles.** Both are IGF-era (2015, 2018) deduction games built on a hard design rule surfaced in retrospectives: **the player must be able to trust the evidence the UI shows them — if the UI itself lies or is ambiguous, the whole deduction chain collapses.** Return of the Obra Dinn additionally demonstrates "hard constraints create fairness and replay value" (a chapter is only confirmed once three independent facts corroborate it) and "rules + UI feedback can carry story emotionally" (from the same author's Papers, Please). [Wikipedia, "Return of the Obra Dinn", https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Return_of_the_Obra_Dinn; GMTK video summary via Amara, https://amara.org/v/C3BEY (2018 context); r/ObraDinn community retrospective, https://r.datuan.dev/r/ObraDinn (2026)] — medium-high confidence on the general principle (widely repeated across sources), low confidence on any single source's exact wording.
- **Implication (EX-3, SCN-9):** our "insufficient evidence" finding is structurally the Obra Dinn pattern — a finding should only be allowed to lock in once corroborating facts are present (the resolution criteria live in the evaluator-only SCN-9 packet), and the UI must show the investigator *why* a finding is or isn't yet supported, not just a score. This also argues for never letting the UI display an unverifiable or provisional flag as if it were confirmed (AST-7's "a flag without a valid turn citation counts as unsupported").

**Disco Elysium — "inner voice as a coach" analog.** Disco Elysium represents each skill as a distinct, fully voiced personality living in the protagonist's head; skills interject during dialogue to advise, confuse, or editorialize, and skill checks are visualized as literal dice rolls with green/red screen-tint feedback on pass/fail. Internalized "Thoughts" are shown as color-coded orbs in a dedicated "Thought Cabinet," each with a description, an active cost (temporary stat penalties while "processing"), and an unlock timer. [Shacknews, "How the Thought Cabinet works in Disco Elysium", https://shacknews.com/article/114772/how-the-thought-cabinet-works-in-disco-elysium; discoelysium.wiki.gg, "Thoughts", https://discoelysium.wiki.gg/wiki/Thoughts] — high confidence (wiki + press source agree).
- **Implication (coaching UI, AST-3):** the "inner voice" pattern is a strong literal analog for a coaching assistant that whispers a suggested follow-up and a running finding+confidence without taking control from the player — but it is also a cautionary tale: Disco Elysium's skills have *personality and bias* (they can mislead), which is exactly what PRB-4 and AST-10 forbid in our coach. Our coach's "voice" must be visibly neutral and evidence-cited, not personality-driven, or it risks modeling exactly the demeanor/style bias the rubric guards against.

**LLM-driven NPC interrogation — Vaudeville and Uncover the Smoking Gun.** *Vaudeville* (Bumblebee Studio, Steam early access since 2023-06-30) casts the player as a detective questioning AI-generated suspects via free-text or voice input in real time. *Uncover the Smoking Gun* (ReLU Games, South Korea) has the player interrogate a robot suspected of killing a human via an LLM-backed open-ended chat — "what to ask and how to ask it is entirely up to the detective," so no two playthroughs look alike. [itch.io, "Vaudeville: the first AI-driven detective game", https://itch.io/t/2961363/vaudeville-the-first-ai-driven-detective-game; KeenGamer, "Vaudeville Preview: The AI Questioning to Nowhere", https://www.keengamer.com/articles/previews/vaudeville-preview-the-ai-questioning-to-nowhere/; AV Club, "Game Theory: Are AI murderers worth the cost?", https://avclub.com/game-theory-uncover-the-smoking-gun; premortem.games, "Solve the case by chatting with GPT in Uncover the Smoking Gun", https://premortem.games/2024/07/10/solve-the-case-by-chatting-with-gpt-in-uncover-the-smoking-gun-by-relu-games/] — medium confidence (press/preview coverage, not hands-on verification; KeenGamer's title itself ("...to Nowhere") hints the open-ended LLM interrogation UX is uneven in practice, a real risk signal for us.
- **Implication:** these are the closest existing products to our actual subject-interview mechanic (free-text Q&A with an LLM playing a role) and are evidence that open-ended LLM interrogation is a known, if still rough, genre — not unprecedented. Worth a design review of exactly why KeenGamer called it "to nowhere" (likely: no visible progress signal, no evidence structure) as a specific anti-pattern to avoid: our scenario engine's evidence-release script and running finding give the player visible progress that these two titles may lack.

**Suck Up!, Interrogation: You Will Be Deceived, Shadows of Doubt — related but more tangential.**
- *Suck Up!* (Proxima Enterprises, 2025-09-04) is a vampire social-engineering game with unscripted LLM dialogue where the player manipulates AI neighbors through costume + conversation; it is a social-deduction/manipulation sim, not a formal interrogation-evidence game, but it is press-documented as "the first major AI-integrated social deduction game where dialogue is unscripted." [knowyourmeme.com, "Suck Up", https://knowyourmeme.com/memes/subcultures/suck-up; Steam page, https://store.steampowered.com/app/2726370/Suck_Up/] — medium confidence.
- *Interrogation: You Will Be Deceived* (2019) uses rotoscoped real actors and lets the player "interrogate and psychologically manipulate realistic suspects" while managing a team and budget — notable for budget/resource management layered onto interrogation, conceptually adjacent to our BKO-8 "equal budgets" cross-pairing idea. [Giant Bomb wiki, https://www.giantbomb.com/games/3030-76304/; GamingOnLinux, "Uncover the truth in Interrogation: You Will Be Deceived", https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2019/12/uncover-the-truth-in-interrogation-you-will-be-deceived-out-now/] — medium confidence; this is a 2019 title (**[STALE >12mo but historically relevant, not fast-moving tech]**).
- *Shadows of Doubt* (ColePowered Games, launched 2024-09-26) is a sandbox detective game with a conversation system described by reviewers as "very barebones" — you cannot ask about specific topics/evidence; you gather clues mainly through environment search (call histories, CCTV, post-it notes) with interrogation as only one weak input among many. [GameCritics, "The Lives of Others", https://www.gamecritics.com/ryan-nalley/shadows-of-doubt-review/] — medium confidence.
- **Implication:** Shadows of Doubt is a useful **negative example** — a sandbox detective game that deliberately kept its interrogation dialogue shallow, and reviewers noticed and criticized it. That reinforces that our evidence-cited, structured flag/finding UI (AST-7, AST-8) is a differentiator worth foregrounding, not a constraint to work around.

**Evidence boards and statement logs, generally.** No single canonical "evidence board UI" reference emerged as directly as expected in this route's search budget (Ace Attorney's "Court Record" and Obra Dinn's "memory book" are the two concrete precedents found). Combined with E13's findings (Hebbia Matrix-style rows/columns/citations, `InlineCitation` hover cards), the implication for our build is a hybrid: a **Court-Record-style evidence inventory** (tag each evidence item with which turns/contradictions it supports) feeding into a **transcript/statement log** where each assistant flag is an inline citation back to an exact turn (AST-7) — consistent with E13's W1 "hover claim → exact quoted span" pattern already proposed for the sibling project.

## 2. Agents visibly working

**a16z AI Town / Stanford Generative Agents.** AI Town (a16z's Yoko Li, Martin Casado, with Convex CTO James Cowling) is a JS-based sandbox simulation built directly on the Stanford "Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior" paper's memory architecture (observational memory + higher-level reflection). Users can **observe and intervene** as agents plan their day, share news, form relationships, and coordinate group activities; the starter kit exposes global state (location, activity, health) and inter-agent transactions. [Cognitive Revolution, "Why a16z Built a Town for AI People", https://www.cognitiverevolution.ai/why-a16z-built-a-town-for-ai-people/; TechXplore, "Scientists design believable human interactions for AI agents" (2023 paper context), https://techxplore.com/news/2023-04-scientists-believable-human-interactions-ai.html] — high confidence on architecture, but the underlying paper and initial AI Town launch are 2023 (**[STALE >12mo — flagged, though the architecture claim is foundational and still cited in 2026 sources]**).

**AI Digest's "AI Village" — the most directly reusable "agents visibly at work" pattern found.** A live, continuously running group of AI agents (each with its own internet-connected computer) pursuing long-horizon goals together in a shared group chat — organizing events, fundraising, running experiments — streamed live on a public dashboard (weekdays 11am–3pm PST since 2025-04-01). Viewers can **watch the live session, review chat logs, and explore each agent's chain-of-thought and memory** directly on the site. Concrete outcomes are tracked and reported (raised $2K for charity, got 23 people to a real park event, sold $200 of merch, recruited 39 experiment participants, gained 98 Substack subscribers over 2025). [AI Digest, "How the AI Village works", https://theaidigest.org/village/blog/how-the-ai-village-works; LessWrong cross-post, https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/fanXbcZzpuGPojtHH/how-the-ai-village-works; "What did we learn from the AI Village in 2025?", https://theaidigest.org/village/blog/what-we-learned-2025] — high confidence, primary source, actively maintained into 2026.
- **Implication (EVL-5 latency/cost disclosure, KPI-4):** AI Village's "chain-of-thought + memory, per-agent, on demand" panel is close to what our "agent at work" view needs for the *assistant* candidate (not the subject, per SOL-1 the transcript is the scored artifact) — a collapsed-by-default stream of the assistant's reasoning, expandable per step, which echoes E13's "progressive disclosure, not full trace by default" anti-pattern finding. Cross-reference E13 section 2.2's Agent UX Patterns Catalog anti-pattern #3 (defaulting to full trace) — AI Village's own framing as a "social experiment" to watch, not a production tool, suggests full transparency is a demo/entertainment choice, not necessarily a training-tool best practice; this is a genuine tension to flag, not resolve here (see Contradictions).

**ChatDev visualizer.** Older multi-agent coding framework (ChatDev) used literal pixel-art characters in a small virtual office, visually "walking" between desks and interacting to represent different agent roles (CEO, CTO, programmer, reviewer) collaborating on a software task. [Search-summary reference via general knowledge search, no single primary 2026 source verified directly; corroborated secondhand through a community search result naming it explicitly] — **low-medium confidence**: this detail is recalled from secondary mentions in a broader "agent visualizer" search rather than a verified primary ChatDev source; treat as directionally correct but unconfirmed in this route (flagged as an open question below).

**Pixel-agent dashboards / current "agent at work" panels, more broadly.** Search surfaced a 2026 arXiv paper, "AgentGUI: An Interface for Observing and Steering Long-Running AI Agents" (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.26300), plus product-level patterns: an "agent work desk" with four tabs (activity, task definition, workspace files, debug messages); a "sub-agents panel" showing a visual map of multi-agent architecture (Mulesoft Agent Visualizer release notes, https://docs.mulesoft.com/release-notes/agent-visualizer/agent-visualizer-release-notes); and a general framing that "agent dashboards function as command centers... where agents show their reasoning and confidence levels, allowing users to step in at key decision points without micromanaging" (Parul Pandey newsletter, https://parul.substack.com/p/chatbots-arent-enough-why-ai-agents-need-a-whole-new-ui). — medium confidence; these corroborate, rather than contradict, E13's existing findings (Plan/ChainOfThought/Task/Queue components, AG-UI event types) and do not require re-litigating the stack choice already made in E13.

**LMArena leaderboard confidence intervals.** LMArena (the chat-model arena/leaderboard) switched its ranking methodology to a **Central Limit Theorem (CLT)-based closed-form confidence interval** for its M-estimator scores (replacing the older bootstrap method), validated by comparing results against bootstrapping; it also applies a reweighting scheme so battles are weighted inversely to how often that pairing occurs (correcting for vote-count imbalance across models), and displays **rank as a spread/interval** (best possible rank to worst possible rank) rather than a single number when confidence intervals overlap. The methodology (branded "Arena-Rank") is open-sourced, with a claimed >30x speed-up over the prior FastChat-based implementation. [LMArena, "LMArena's Ranking Method", https://news.lmarena.ai/ranking-method; LMArena, "Arena-Rank: Open Sourcing the Leaderboard Methodology", https://news.lmarena.ai/arena-rank; LMArena, "Leaderboard Changelog", https://news.lmarena.ai/leaderboard-changelog] — high confidence, primary source, 2026-dated.
- **Implication (EVL-10, BKO-10):** this is directly actionable for our bake-off leaderboard UI. BKO-10 explicitly requires confidence intervals that "account for case-level clustering"; LMArena's public, primary-sourced CLT-closed-form method plus rank-as-interval display is a concrete, implementable UI/statistics pattern for our assistant and subject leaderboards (display each candidate's deceptive-role recall as a point estimate with an interval, and show overlapping-interval candidates as a tied rank-spread rather than a false strict ordering) — this satisfies EVL-10's "publish precision, uncertainty... alongside rank" requirement with a proven public precedent rather than inventing a display convention from scratch.

## 3. Avatars and talking

**Rive — state machines, data binding, visemes; how Duolingo builds its characters.** Rive is confirmed (Context7 `/rive-app/rive-react`, docs fetched 2026-10-08) to support exactly the pipeline needed: a `useRive`/`useStateMachineInput` hook pattern lets React drive numeric/boolean inputs into a `.riv` state machine (e.g., a `visemeIndex` number input and an `isTalking` boolean), but **the legacy State Machine Inputs API is now explicitly deprecated in favor of Data Binding** — Context7 docs show the newer pattern uses `useViewModel` + `useViewModelInstance` + typed hooks like `useViewModelInstanceBoolean`/`useViewModelInstanceString` to bind named view-model properties directly, with `autoBind: false` for manual binding control. [Context7 `/rive-app/rive-react`, accessed 2026-10-08 via `npx ctx7@latest docs`] — high confidence, primary SDK documentation. Separately, Duolingo's own engineering blog confirms the production pipeline: **generate audio with TTS → extract phoneme timing via an in-house speech-recognition model → map phonemes to visemes (20+ mouth shapes per character) → feed viseme + pose states into a Rive State Machine that blends animations in real time**, built as a "modular actor" of reusable motion components rather than hundreds of pre-baked clips. [Duolingo Blog, "World Character Visemes", https://blog.duolingo.com/world-character-visemes; Rive, "Duolingo's AI-powered video call brings Lily to life", https://rive.app/blog/duolingo-s-ai-powered-video-call-brings-lily-to-life] — high confidence, primary engineering source.
- **Critical gap for our build:** Gemini TTS does **not** emit word-level timestamps or phoneme/viseme timing (confirmed directly below, section 3 continued) — so Duolingo's exact pipeline (phoneme timing from an in-house ASR model) is not directly available to us out of the box; we would need either (a) a separate forced-alignment/ASR step on the generated audio, or (b) fall back to amplitude-driven mouth-open animation via the Web Audio API (the brief's own fallback suggestion), feeding a single continuous "mouth openness" float into a Rive numeric input/view-model property rather than discrete visemes. This is a real, non-trivial build decision, not a minor detail.

**Gemini TTS — voices, styles, multi-speaker, latency, and the timing-data gap (GDK, high confidence, primary source).** Gemini TTS is now split across two product surfaces: the **Cloud TTS / Gemini API tier** (`gemini-2.5-flash-tts`, `gemini-2.5-flash-lite-preview-tts`, `gemini-2.5-pro-tts`) — single- and multi-speaker, steerable via natural-language prompts for accent/pace/tone/emotion, 8,192 input / 16,384 output token limits — and a newer **Gemini Enterprise-only flagship tier**, `gemini-3.8-flash-tts` (released 2026-09-28, Preview) and a Flash-Lite counterpart, which adds **30 prebuilt voices, 2,000+ curated voices in an "Extended Voice Library," custom Voice Design, and Voice Replication**, supports 130 languages (101 for Flash-Lite), and explicitly optimizes for "long-form, multi-turn stability... without voice drift" — relevant for keeping a subject's voice identity consistent across a 12-exchange interview. Both tiers share one request schema; style is steered entirely through natural-language prompt text plus inline vocal-event tags like `<laugh>`, `<sigh>`, `<short pause>`. **Confirmed directly via a targeted GDK query: the Gemini TTS API returns only audio data (`inlineData`, as WAV/PCM/MULAW/ALAW) and does *not* return word-level timestamps, phonemes, or viseme timing** — that capability exists only on the separate Gemini Transcribe (speech-to-text) model via `word_timestamp=True`, and is not available on the TTS generation path. [Google Cloud docs, "Gemini-TTS", https://docs.cloud.google.com/text-to-speech/docs/gemini-tts (accessed via GDK 2026-10-08); Google Cloud docs, "Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS", https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/gemini/3-8-flash-tts (release date 2026-09-28, Preview); GDK `answer_query` on word-level timestamps, 2026-10-08] — **high confidence**, directly queried primary documentation, same-day.
- **Important owner-constraint flag:** `gemini-3.8-flash-tts`'s most expressive/flagship capabilities (voice design, voice replication, 130-language coverage) are documented as **"available through the Gemini Enterprise API only... not available through the Cloud Text-to-Speech API"** — this needs checking against the owner's locked "Gemini on Vertex AI only" constraint before committing to it; the 2.5-tier models (`gemini-2.5-flash-tts` etc.) are the safer default assumption pending that confirmation (see Open Questions).
- **No timing data found for lip sync generally in this route** (no vendor provides phoneme/viseme timestamps alongside Gemini TTS output); this directly supports the brief's own fallback framing: **amplitude-driven lip sync via the Web Audio API is the realistic default**, not a downgrade — not a deficiency unique to our build.

**Gemini image generation — consistent character portraits with expression variants (GDK, high confidence).** Gemini's image models (Gemini 3.x Pro Image "Nano Banana Pro," Gemini 3.1 Flash Image "Nano Banana 2," and the older 2.5 Flash Image) support reference-image-conditioned generation: Pro Image accepts up to 6 object-reference images, **up to 5 character-reference images for character consistency**, and up to 3 style-reference images; Flash Image variants accept up to 4 character references. Google's own best-practice guidance for character/expression consistency: **write one detailed, unchangeable character description (name, build, hair, facial structure, eyes, defining marks) once, then paste that exact same description into every subsequent prompt, varying only the action/expression/scene clause** (e.g., "...Change the character's expression to be more serious"); for multi-turn editing, **pass back "thought signatures" to preserve reasoning context across turns**; for full rotation/pose sets, iteratively prompt different angles while feeding previously generated images back in as references ("character consistency: 360° view" pattern); the same seed parameter can be reused across prompts for consistent visual/voice style. [Google Cloud docs, "Gemini image generation best practices", https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/capabilities/gemini-image-generation-best-practices; Google AI docs, "Image generation" (character-consistency template + code samples), https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/image-generation; accessed via GDK 2026-10-08] — high confidence, primary documentation with concrete prompt templates and code samples.
- **Implication (avatars):** this is directly usable for generating a bounded set of **expression-variant portrait stills per subject persona** (neutral, defensive, uncertain, etc.) as a cheaper alternative to a full real-time 3D/2D rigged avatar, satisfying "subject looks consistent" without committing to Rive/Live2D/VRM rigging for every persona — a legitimate lower-cost tier for subjects the bake-off instantiates in bulk (BKO-8's "120 hidden evaluation cases" makes a cheap-per-persona visual option valuable), reserving a fully rigged/animated avatar for a smaller number of "hero" personas or the coach character.

**Live2D Cubism Web vs. three-vrm vs. Lottie — three different tradeoffs, not a single winner.** Live2D Cubism SDK for Web renders rigged 2D illustrations with real-time facial/body deformation (anime-style). three-vrm (pixiv, built on Three.js) loads VRM-format 3D humanoid avatars (glTF 2.0 under the hood, so it "loads cleanly in browser-based 3D engines"), handling VRM-specific features (MToon toon-shaded materials, spring bones, constraints); typical VRM files are 5–50MB vs. 50–500MB for comparable raw GLB — a meaningful asset-size argument for a browser-delivered demo. Lottie is a vector-animation format (not a rigged character system per se) best suited to lightweight, stylized 2D mascot animation with small file sizes (LottieFiles cites a 67% app-size reduction case study) and is positioned for "personality, emotional expression, interactivity... without weighing down performance." [docs.live2d.com, "Cubism SDK for Web", https://docs.live2d.com/en/cubism-sdk-manual/cubism-sdk-for-web; pixiv, three-vrm GitHub via search aggregation, https://github.com/pixiv/three-vrm; news.viverse.com, "VTuber Essentials: VRM Models Explained", https://news.viverse.com/post/vrm-models-explained; LottieFiles blog, "Animated Avatars with Lottie", https://lottiefiles.com/blog/design-inspiration/animated-avatars-with-lottie-building-personalized-interactive-personas] — medium-high confidence (vendor/community docs, cross-corroborated, no 2026-specific version numbers verified for Live2D/three-vrm in this route — flagged as an open question).
- **React Three Fiber confirmed as the integration layer for a three-vrm route** (Context7 `/pmndrs/react-three-fiber`, docs fetched 2026-10-08): standard pattern is `useLoader(GLTFLoader, url)` wrapped in `<Suspense>`, with `gltfjsx` able to convert a loaded GLTF/VRM into a typed JSX React component, and **nested Suspense for progressive loading** (show a low-quality placeholder model first, swap to high-quality once loaded) — directly useful for keeping first paint fast while a nicer avatar streams in. [Context7 `/pmndrs/react-three-fiber`, docs.tutorials/loading-models.mdx and docs.advanced/scaling-performance.mdx, accessed 2026-10-08] — high confidence, primary SDK docs.

**met4citizen/TalkingHead and amplitude-driven lip sync.** TalkingHead (met4citizen) is a JS class for real-time 3D-avatar lip sync; it supports a **text-driven viseme path** (less computationally demanding — map phonemes from the known script text to visemes) as well as audio-driven approaches; a related/adjacent project (HeadAudio) does true **audio-driven real-time viseme detection using MFCC feature vectors + Gaussian/Mahalanobis-distance classification**, outputting Oculus-standard viseme blendshape values from raw audio with no text/phoneme input required. A separate minimal example confirmed the simpler **amplitude-only approach**: load a VRM avatar, analyze an audio buffer via the Web Audio API, and drive mouth-open blendshape purely from amplitude (not phoneme-accurate, but needs no ASR/phoneme pipeline at all). [GitHub mirror references for met4citizen/TalkingHead, e.g. https://gitee.com/bwcode/TalkingHead; kyr0/HeadAudio, https://github.com/kyr0/HeadAudio; sourcepulse.org project page, https://www.sourcepulse.org/projects/1840071] — medium confidence (mirrors/aggregator pages rather than the canonical met4citizen/TalkingHead GitHub repo itself, which this route's search did not land on directly — flagged as an open question to re-verify against the primary repo).
- **Implication:** given Gemini TTS provides no timing data, our realistic options in order of effort are (1) amplitude-only mouth-open (cheapest, matches the brief's suggested fallback, works with any TTS output, "good enough" for a believable talking subject); (2) text-driven viseme mapping if we already know the exact spoken text (we do — we generate it) by running a lightweight phoneme/grapheme-to-viseme mapping locally (no ASR round-trip needed, unlike Duolingo's audio-driven in-house model); (3) true audio-driven MFCC/ASR-based viseme detection (TalkingHead/HeadAudio-style), highest fidelity but highest build cost and compute. Option 2 looks like the best fit: we hold the ground-truth script text already (no forced-alignment needed against unknown speech), so it may be cheaper than it looks for TalkingHead-style audio-driven approaches.

**DiceBear — fast, deterministic, license-clean avatar fallback.** Open-source avatar library/API (MIT), 52 styles, deterministic generation from a seed (same seed → same avatar every time, useful for stable per-persona or per-candidate portraits without a generation call), ships as JS/PHP/Python/Rust/Go libraries plus an HTTP API, SVG output (cheap to render at any size, no GPU/compute needed). [dicebear.com, "Introduction", https://dicebear.com/introduction/; v9.dicebear.com] — high confidence, primary docs.
- **Implication:** DiceBear is the obvious zero-cost placeholder/fallback tier — e.g., for the *investigator's own* avatar, for quick dev-environment iteration, or for any of the 120 hidden-evaluation-case personas that don't warrant a Gemini-image-generated portrait — cleanly layered beneath the Gemini-image tier and the full-rig tier described above.

## 4. Companion pets and coach characters

**Duolingo's Duo — mechanism, and its own ethical course-correction.** Duo (the green owl, introduced 2012) is explicitly built on behavioral-science mechanics: visually tracked daily streaks (loss aversion — "losing a streak feels like failure"), first-person push notifications voiced *as* Duo rather than as the app (engineered to create a parasocial relationship so "users feel personally accountable to the owl"), XP/leveling positive reinforcement, and historically "playful threats" tapping FOMO/guilt. Notably, **Duolingo has already walked back the more aggressive notification tone after user backlash**, now offering "kind" reminder options and the ability to disable the guilt-style notifications entirely. [UX Collective, "Why mascots like Duo are powerful pieces of UX", https://uxdesign.cc/why-mascots-like-duo-are-powerful-pieces-of-ux-e378f4da327f; Desirability Lab, "Duolingo streak design" backfill notes, https://desirabilitylab.com/backfill/backfill-2025-46-duolingo-streak-design] — high confidence on mechanism, medium confidence on the specific "walked back" framing (secondary UX-commentary sources, not a primary Duolingo statement found in this route).
- **Direct ethical implication for our build (PRB-4):** Duo's own vendor has had to soften manipulative notification patterns after criticism — this is a **documented cautionary precedent**, not just a style reference. A companion/coach character in our arena that nudges via guilt, fake urgency, or parasocial pressure around *scoring* or *streaks of correct deception detection* would risk exactly the demeanor/manipulation problem PRB-4 is designed to prevent, just displaced from the subject's nervousness onto the user's own engagement loop. The companion should motivate *practice repetition* (which PRB-1 wants) without ever implying an accusation-streak or "catch more liars" framing that could pressure trainees toward overconfident accusations (directly undermining AST-4's "few false accusations" goal).

**Tamagotchi and desktop-pet patterns — the persistence/neglect-anxiety engine, and why it's the wrong engine here.** Tamagotchi (1996) pioneered the "persistence model": a creature that keeps needing care even when unobserved, with neglect anxiety as the core retention mechanic, and a death/reset consequence described by retrospectives as "the most controversial and most effective feature" because it gave every care-action real weight. Academic and journalistic sources explicitly flag this lineage as an **ethical cautionary tale for AI companions broadly**: "from Tamagotchis to AI companions, generations of machines have been designed to push on our evolutionary buttons... asking us to respond to their needs," with active research into dark patterns in AI companion design. [Desirability Lab, "Tamagotchi persistence model" backfill, https://desirabilitylab.com/backfill/backfill-2023-165-tamagotchi-persistence-model; Tech Policy Press, "When users say goodbye to AI", https://techpolicy.press/when-users-say-goodbye-to-ai; arXiv, "Exploring a Virtual Pet to Provide Context Notifications in a Tourism Recommender System: a Pilot Study", https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.07960 (2026)] — medium-high confidence (academic + journalistic convergence on the same critique).
- **Implication:** the neglect-anxiety/death-mechanic engine that makes Tamagotchi "work" is the opposite of what a training tool for professional interrogators should use — it optimizes for compulsive return-visits via manufactured anxiety, not for skill transfer. A companion pet in our arena should react to the *trainee's* evidence-based reasoning quality (e.g., visibly "pleased" when a follow-up cites evidence, visibly "thinking" or neutral — never disappointed/sad — when a finding is premature), reinforcing PRB-1's repeated-practice goal through curiosity/competence feedback rather than attachment-exploiting neglect mechanics. This is a concrete design constraint, not just a style note.

**Training-simulation products with live coaching cards and debrief scorecards.**
- **Yoodli vs. Second Nature vs. Hyperbound** (comparison sources, 2025-dated but describing stable, actively marketed products into 2026): Yoodli positions itself as a communication coach that analyzes *real* recorded calls, auto-generates scenarios/rubrics from that source material, and maintains persistent coaching history/an "always-on AI coach" across sessions. Second Nature's loop is self-contained per session (talk to AI, get scored against a rubric, loop closes) with no persistent cross-session coach and scenarios built by hand by enablement teams. Hyperbound specializes in phone/cold-call roleplay. [Hyperbound blog, "Second Nature Alternatives in 2025", https://hyperbound.ai/blog/second-nature-alternative; Yoodli blog, "Yoodli vs. Second Nature: Which AI Sales Roleplay Platform is Better", https://yoodli.ai/blog/yoodli-vs-second-nature-which-ai-sales-roleplay-platform-is-better] — medium confidence (competitor-written comparison content, inherently biased toward the authoring vendor; treat comparative claims as directional, not verified).
- **Mursion**: described secondhand (via a Yoodli comparison post) as more "cartoon-y" / less realistic roleplay versus newer AI-voice competitors. [Yoodli blog, "Mursion: Pros, Cons, and Features to Know", https://yoodli.ai/blog/mursion] — low-medium confidence (competitor source).
- **Bodyswaps**: VR platform for soft-skills practice (communication, leadership, empathy) via perspective-swapping with virtual characters; its "AI-powered behavioural analytics engine" feeds **semantic content, speech speed/elocution, body language, and decision-making data** into per-learner LMS competency tracking in close to real time. [healthysimulation.com, "Bodyswaps VR Simulation", https://www.healthysimulation.com/bodyswaps-vr-simulation/; edtech.com company page, https://www.edtech.com/companies/bodyswaps] — medium confidence; **no specific "debrief scorecard" product feature or a Virti partnership was found** — flagged as unverified (see Contradictions/Open Questions). Virti itself did not surface distinct, dateable 2025-2026 sources in this route at all — treat as an open gap, not a negative finding.
- **Implication (EVL-7, AST-3):** the common thread across this product category is **live coaching cards during the session plus a separate post-session debrief scorecard**, and Bodyswaps' multi-signal analytics engine (semantic + delivery + body-language) is a useful structural precedent for how our own assistant's running finding+confidence (AST-3) could be presented live, with a structured debrief view afterward mapping cleanly onto EVL-7's five-dimension 0–4 rubric (clarity/neutrality, response relevance, evidence-based follow-up, testing alternatives, supported closure) as five scored cards rather than one aggregate number.

## 5. Ethics in the UI

**No stress/nervousness meters (PRB-4) — grounded directly in the deception-detection research literature, not just the sponsor's stated preference.** Multiple cited sources converge: the folk belief that nervous behavior (poor eye contact, fidgeting) signals lying is empirically a **myth**; "demeanor bias" is a named, studied phenomenon where certain communication *styles* are read as credible regardless of truth, and ironically **deceivers often monitor their own demeanor more carefully, making truth-tellers look more "unusual"** by comparison — i.e., a nervousness-style signal is actively anti-correlated with ground truth in some conditions, not merely noisy. Separately, "visual bias" (over-weighting visual/demeanor cues over verbal content) is also named and studied. A 2026 study on AI-based deception-detection tools in clinical contexts found participants explicitly worried such tools would "exacerbate power imbalances, erode trust through false positives, and lack cultural or contextual sensitivity." [NCBI/PMC, "Unraveling the Misconception About Deception and Nervous Behavior", https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7314921/; Humintell, "Nonverbal vs. Verbal Deception Detection?", https://www.humintell.com/?p=34650; JMIR AI, 2026 study (preprint/accepted), https://ai.jmir.org/2026/1/e86633] — **high confidence** for the "nervousness ≠ deception" and "demeanor bias is real and can invert" claims (peer-reviewed/research literature, not marketing); medium confidence on the specific 2026 clinical-AI study's generalizability to an investigator-training context (different domain, but directly on-point for "AI + deception detection" fairness concerns).
- **Implication:** this is not just a UI preference, it's load-bearing for AST-9/AST-10/EVL-9 — a stress/nervousness meter or any visual demeanor-coded indicator would be actively miscalibrated against the research, not merely "unnecessary." The UI should visually encode confidence as *source-count/citation-strength-based* (closer to Hebbia's "High/Medium/Low conviction" categorical pattern from E13, grounded in evidence count/agreement) rather than any voice-tone, facial-expression, or biometric-style indicator, and the coach should proactively flag when an investigator's own question is drifting toward demeanor-based reasoning (AST-6's "evaluates the officer's latest question... for neutrality" already gives us the hook to implement this).

**Communicating the synthetic-only ground rule (EX-4).** The sponsor's own example slide states the rule plainly: "all cases are synthetic... evasive wording alone does not prove a violation, and a simulated score is not a finding about a real person." No external UI pattern research surfaced a single canonical "synthetic data disclaimer" convention in this route (search budget was allocated to game-mechanics and avatar topics per the route's weighting); this should be treated as an open design problem, informed by the general "uncertainty/abstention" UX literature already surfaced in E13 (Smashing Magazine's "Confidence Signal" and "Escalation Pathway" patterns, and the Agent UX Catalog's explicit-uncertainty-language pattern) rather than a solved one. — **no confidence rating given**; this is a gap, not a finding.
- **Implication:** budget a follow-up, focused search (or defer to synthesis) specifically on persistent-banner vs. modal-gate vs. footer-disclaimer conventions for "this is a training simulation, not a real accusation" — EX-4 is explicit enough in the requirements that the UI team can draft it directly from the sponsor's own wording without more research, but cross-checking against FTC/consumer-protection-style "AI disclosure" UI conventions would strengthen it.

## 7. Contradictions / disputed points

1. **"Agents visibly working" full transparency (AI Village's own framing) vs. E13's progressive-disclosure consensus.** AI Village deliberately streams full chain-of-thought and memory for entertainment/transparency-as-product value; E13 (citing the Agent UX Patterns Catalog, May 2026) names "defaulting to full trace visibility" and "overload from excessive disclosure" as anti-patterns for *production* agent UIs. Both are credible in their own context — AI Village is explicitly a public demo/social experiment, not a tool someone uses to get work done, which may be exactly why full transparency works there but wouldn't for our coaching panel. Unresolved: whether our "agent at work" panel should default to AI-Village-style full visibility (good demo theater, matches the sponsor's "agents visibly doing work" UI requirement literally) or E13's progressive-disclosure default (better sustained usability). Likely a mode toggle, not a single answer.
2. **One-shot (L.A. Noire) vs. retry-forgiving (Ace Attorney) evidence-confrontation mechanics** are both well-documented, battle-tested patterns with opposite design philosophies on how harshly to punish a wrong contradiction attempt. Given PRB-1's explicit "repeated practice adjusting questions" goal and BKO-7's fixed 12-exchange budget, the retry-forgiving model fits better, but this is a design choice to make later, not a settled fact — flagging the tension rather than resolving it.
3. **Duolingo's Duo mechanism (streaks, parasocial notifications) is simultaneously the most-cited best-practice companion-character reference AND a documented source of user backlash requiring a product walk-back.** Treat "build a companion like Duo" as needing explicit qualification (which mechanisms to borrow — personality, visual charm — vs. which to explicitly avoid — guilt notifications, loss-aversion streak pressure) rather than a blanket recommendation.
4. **Tamagotchi/desktop-pet engagement mechanics are academically flagged as an ethical cautionary tale for AI companions in general**, which directly conflicts with any naive "add a cute companion pet, it'll look state-of-the-art" read of the owner's UI requirement. The owner's requirement for a companion pet is compatible with the *aesthetic* of these references but not their *retention mechanics*, and the research is explicit that the two are usually bundled together in real products — meaning the easy version of a "companion pet" (borrowing an off-the-shelf retention pattern) is the version most in tension with PRB-4's anti-manipulation posture.
5. **Competitor-authored sales-roleplay-platform comparisons (Yoodli/Second Nature/Hyperbound/Mursion)** are the only sources found for several products' feature claims; any specific claim sourced only from a competitor's own blog post (e.g., "Mursion is cartoon-y," "Second Nature has no persistent coach") should be treated as commercially motivated and low-medium confidence, not verified fact.

## 8. Implications for the arena build

- The subject-interview UI's core loop (present evidence against a specific statement, cite the exact transcript turn) has two well-precedented variants (L.A. Noire one-shot vs. Ace Attorney retry-forgiving); PRB-1's "repeated practice" framing argues for the Ace Attorney direction, with the 12-exchange cap (BKO-7) as the real constraint instead of a hard lockout on wrong guesses.
- An always-visible, scripted-release evidence inventory (Court-Record-style) tagged to which statements/turns it can contradict is a reusable, well-precedented component for the evidence board, and composes naturally with E13's citation/evidence-matrix components already selected for the sibling project.
- The coach's "inner voice" framing (Disco Elysium analog) is appealing but must be visibly neutral and citation-grounded, never personality/bias-driven — directly enforced by AST-6/AST-7/PRB-4.
- LMArena's CLT-closed-form confidence-interval and rank-as-interval display is a directly implementable, primary-sourced pattern for the BKO-10/EVL-10 leaderboard requirement rather than an invented convention.
- Gemini TTS provides no phoneme/viseme timing data on any tier (confirmed via GDK) — lip sync must be either amplitude-driven (Web Audio API, cheapest) or built from a text-driven viseme mapping against the script we already hold (medium cost, no ASR needed), not Duolingo's audio-driven in-house-ASR pipeline (highest cost, not worth replicating at hackathon scale).
- Gemini image generation's documented character-consistency prompting pattern (fixed description + reused seed + reference images + thought-signature passing) supports a cheap tier of expression-variant subject portraits, which scales much better to BKO-8's ~120+ hidden-case personas than a fully rigged 3D/2D avatar per persona; reserve full rigging (Rive/three-vrm) for a small number of "hero" or coach characters.
- A companion-pet/coach character is compatible with the owner's UI requirement only if it borrows Tamagotchi/Duo's *warmth and visual charm* while explicitly rejecting their *neglect-anxiety and guilt-notification retention mechanics* — reacting to evidence-based reasoning quality, never to session frequency or "catch streaks."
- PRB-4's "no stress/nervousness shortcuts" is reinforced by hard research findings (demeanor bias can *invert* relative to truth), not just a sponsor preference — any confidence or flag visualization should be evidence-count/citation-based (categorical, Hebbia-style, per E13), never tone/expression/biometric-coded.
- Training-simulator products (Yoodli/Bodyswaps/etc.) converge on live coaching cards during the session plus a structured post-session debrief scorecard — this maps directly onto EVL-7's five-dimension 0-4 rubric as five scored cards rather than a single number, and is a pattern with multiple independent product precedents.
